question: A solid blue line on a sectional chart marks the edge of:
option_a: Class B airspace
option_b: Class C airspace
option_c: Class D airspace
option_d: Class E airspace

question: You plan to fly inside a dashed blue ring. Before you launch, you need:
option_a: ATC authorization, usually through LAANC
option_b: Nothing, as long as you stay below 400 feet
option_c: A phone call to the airport manager only
option_d: A NOTAM filed with the FAA for that day

question: A dashed magenta ring around a small airport means the airspace there:
option_a: Is Class E, starting at the surface
option_b: Is Class E, starting at 700 feet
option_c: Is Class D, with a part-time tower
option_d: Is Class G, under an approach path

question: You are inside a faded magenta band with no other ring drawn. Flying at 300 feet AGL, you are in:
option_a: Class G, since that Class E starts at 700 ft
option_b: Class E, so you need LAANC before you fly
option_c: Class D, since magenta marks a towered field
option_d: Class C, since the band is its outer shelf

question: An airspace ring is labeled 70 over 25. That piece of airspace runs from:
option_a: 2,500 to 7,000 feet MSL
option_b: 25 to 70 feet above the ground
option_c: 2,500 to 7,000 feet AGL
option_d: 250 to 700 feet MSL

question: A Class B shelf is labeled 80 over 30. The ground below is at 1,000 ft MSL. Your drone at 400 ft AGL is:
option_a: Below the shelf, about 1,600 feet under it
option_b: Inside the shelf, so you need authorization
option_c: Above the shelf, so you need authorization
option_d: Right at the floor of the shelf, at 3,000 ft

question: The ground at an airport is 1,000 ft MSL. Your drone at 400 ft AGL there is at about:
option_a: 1,400 feet MSL
option_b: 600 feet MSL
option_c: 400 feet MSL
option_d: 1,000 feet MSL

question: The bottom number on an airspace ring reads SFC. For a drone pilot, this means:
option_a: The airspace reaches the ground where you stand
option_b: The numbers on that ring are measured in AGL
option_c: The airspace has no floor and no fixed ceiling
option_d: The airspace is closed to every drone flight

question: An obstruction is labeled 1240 with (380) beneath it. How tall is the tower?
option_a: 380 feet
option_b: 1,240 feet
option_c: 860 feet
option_d: 1,620 feet

question: The same obstruction reads 1240 over (380). The ground at its base is at about:
option_a: 860 feet MSL
option_b: 380 feet MSL
option_c: 1,240 feet MSL
option_d: 1,620 feet MSL

question: An obstruction reads 1910 over (470). Flying at your legal maximum near it, you:
option_a: Must go around it, since it is taller than 400 ft
option_b: May fly over it, since 1,910 is above your limit
option_c: May fly over it, since it is under 500 feet AGL
option_d: Must land, since any obstruction ends the flight

question: Starburst marks drawn around the top of an obstruction symbol mean the obstruction:
option_a: Has lights on it at night
option_b: Is over 1,000 feet AGL
option_c: Is a group of several towers
option_d: Has guy-wires attached

question: A guyed tower is more dangerous than its chart symbol suggests because:
option_a: Its cables reach far out and are not charted
option_b: Its height is shown in MSL rather than AGL
option_c: Its symbol is drawn smaller than the real tower
option_d: Its warning lights are turned off in daylight

question: A blue airport symbol on a sectional chart tells you the airport:
option_a: Has a control tower
option_b: Has no control tower
option_c: Is a private field
option_d: Has only turf runways

question: An airport's text block reads 1129 L 40 122.8. The longest runway is about:
option_a: 4,000 feet long
option_b: 40 feet long
option_c: 1,129 feet long
option_d: 400 feet long

question: An R inside an airport symbol means the airport:
option_a: Is private, and permission is required
option_b: Has a radar-equipped control tower
option_c: Sits in restricted military airspace
option_d: Has runway lights available all night

question: In the middle of a chart grid square there is a large 3 with a small 5 beside it. This tells you:
option_a: Its highest terrain or obstacle is near 3,500 ft MSL
option_b: Its airspace ceiling is 3,500 feet above the ground
option_c: You may fly up to 350 feet AGL anywhere in that square
option_d: Its magnetic variation is about 3.5 degrees east

question: An area outlined with hatching and labeled R-5503 is:
option_a: Restricted airspace, entered only with permission
option_b: A Class B shelf that starts at 5,503 feet MSL
option_c: A recommended route for low-flying aircraft
option_d: A practice area open to any drone below 400 feet

question: Flying in Class G airspace, you:
option_a: Need no authorization, but all Part 107 rules apply
option_b: Need no authorization, and may fly above 400 feet
option_c: Need LAANC, since airspace near people is controlled
option_d: Need a NOTAM filed before every single flight

question: The FAA UAS Facility Map shows 100 in your grid square. Your maximum altitude there is:
option_a: 100 feet AGL
option_b: 400 feet AGL
option_c: 100 feet MSL
option_d: 1,000 feet AGL

question: A Facility Map grid square right off the end of a runway shows 0. This means:
option_a: No flight there is pre-approved through LAANC
option_b: You may fly at any height there without asking
option_c: The ceiling is unknown, so 400 feet applies
option_d: You may fly there only between sunset and sunrise

question: LAANC lets a remote pilot:
option_a: Get fast approval in controlled airspace
option_b: Fly higher than 400 feet near busy airports
option_c: Skip the preflight check near an airport
option_d: Register a drone heavier than 55 pounds

question: The general Part 107 altitude limit for a small drone is:
option_a: 400 feet AGL
option_b: 400 feet MSL
option_c: 500 feet AGL
option_d: 1,200 feet AGL

question: A drone is hovering perfectly in place. Which is true?
option_a: Lift equals weight
option_b: Lift is greater than weight
option_c: Thrust is greater than drag
option_d: Weight is greater than lift

question: Diagonal motor pairs on a quadcopter spin the same direction so that:
option_a: The torques cancel, so the drone holds heading
option_b: The drone can fly faster in a straight line
option_c: All four props push air in the same direction
option_d: The battery drains evenly across the motors

question: To yaw, a quadcopter:
option_a: Speeds up one diagonal pair and slows the other
option_b: Speeds up the front pair and slows the back pair
option_c: Speeds up the left pair and slows the right pair
option_d: Speeds up all four motors at exactly the same rate

question: When you push forward from a hover, the drone dips slightly because:
option_a: Tilting turns part of the lift into thrust instead
option_b: The back motors slow down to tip the nose forward
option_c: Air moving under the props cuts their thrust a lot
option_d: The battery voltage drops as motors work

question: Rolling to the right is a rotation around the:
option_a: Longitudinal axis, nose to tail
option_b: Lateral axis, wingtip to wingtip
option_c: Vertical axis, top to bottom
option_d: Diagonal axis, motor to motor

question: A LiPo battery pack has started to swell. You should:
option_a: Retire it and stop using it
option_b: Fly it once more, then retire it
option_c: Charge it fully to settle the cells
option_d: Store it fully charged until it flattens

question: A battery you will not use for two weeks should be:
option_a: Left at storage charge
option_b: Left at full charge
option_c: Drained completely flat
option_d: Left inside the aircraft
